purpose: Capture high-value primary-report leads for the Pared River Catchment freshwater fish baseline while keeping aggregate counts separate from named taxa, station-level occurrences, current distribution, protected-area boundaries and public-use permissions.

project.name: Karayan Ket Agbiag / River is Life; Darwin Initiative project 31-005, Socially and ecologically coherent freshwater protection in Northern Philippines
partnersAsReported: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
Department of Agriculture — Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources

fishSpeciesCountsAsReportedElsewhereInSa.sourceWording: A total of 4 invasive fish species and 10 native species identified.

biologicalSurvey.countReconciliation: The report separately gives 6/15/8 aquatic-species counts by municipality and 10 native plus 4 invasive fish species in its monitoring section. The category, overlap, and counting basis are not explained well enough to reconcile these figures or derive a catchment checklist.

laterMonitoringLead.interpretation: This documents a fish-tagging progress count, not eight named public occurrence records. The report does not establish how the tagged taxa relate to the ten native fish species reported in the annual report.

sanctuarySiteCrosswalkLead.discrepancy: The BFAR report says 10 potential sites but its narrative contains 11 named locality mentions across these three groups. It does not clarify whether a named sitio/falls is nested within another site or which mentions form one site.

annexesReferencedByDarwinReport: Annex 12 digital Pared River and land-use maps

evidenceLimits: Aggregate counts do not identify any fish taxon; no species checklist, accepted-name crosswalk, voucher, photo, capture event or taxon-by-station result was retrieved.
Municipal totals do not show which species occurred in which municipality and cannot be used to infer presence or absence at any particular reach.

The report uses different aggregate descriptions (municipality-level aquatic-species counts; native/invasive fish counts; later tagged-native-species count) whose definitions and overlap are not resolved.
Survey station count and river kilometre summaries are not coordinates or reusable river geometry.
The BFAR locality mentions and proposed sanctuary count are not legal boundaries, current fishing rules or proof that each sanctuary has the same status today.
The report/download pages reviewed did not state item-specific reuse permissions for the underlying species data, survey tables, GIS maps or sanctuary geometry.
nextAction: Locate or request Darwin project 31-005 Annex 9 and the full ecological assessment; ask ZSL/BFAR/DENR or partner LGUs for the accepted fish checklist, native/invasive category, survey dates and methods, per-municipality and station crosswalk, voucher/photo IDs, sampling effort, generalized or precise coordinates as they are authorized to release, data dictionary, maps/CRS, and written terms for citation, redistribution and map/data reuse. Separately resolve the 6/15/8 versus 10+4 count bases and the 10-site versus 11 locality-mention discrepancy. Do not publish taxon or geometry rows until source-level verification and reuse review are complete.

sources.supports: BFAR Region 02 reports a ZSL aquatic assessment on Pared River across Alcala, Baggao and Peñablanca; says ten potential freshwater sanctuary sites were identified; lists locality mentions; and reports fish-species identification work, but gives no taxa or survey results.

Year-one report gives 32-barangay/59.5-km biological survey coverage, 23 transects, 170 stations, municipality-level aquatic-species counts and a separate total of ten native plus four invasive fish species. It references the underlying assessment and GIS annexes but the reviewed report does not name taxa or publish station-level records.
Half-year report for April–September 2025 says 172 fish individuals were VIE-tagged from eight native species; no species names, individual records, capture sites or coordinates are published.
